interpretation: Instruction: 'Pick the salad dressing and place it in the basket'. Robot: capx_libero_panda (7-joint Panda, parallel-jaw gripper, 0.079 m max width, closing along TCP x, approach along TCP z; cameras agentview (scene) and robot0_eye_in_hand (wrist)). The salad dressing is the dark glass bottle with a green label and black cap, standing near the robot at about (0.402, -0.080). Perception first gave it as obj1 (6x4x14 cm, top z 0.148) and later split it into body obj1 + cap obj13, which I merged into one agent object (obj17). It is about 14.2 cm tall and about 6.1 cm wide at the body (z 0.02-0.07). The upper part and cap are about 3.4-3.9 cm wide. The basket is obj7, a woven basket with a white cloth liner at about (0.61, 0.26): rim z 0.144, liner floor z about 0.01-0.02, flat floor about x 0.58-0.635, y 0.215-0.325, with the liner sloping up to the rim. Goal state: the salad dressing bottle resting inside the basket, released by the gripper, with no other object disturbed. There was nothing ambiguous: only one bottle matches salad dressing (the other bottle, obj5/obj6 and later obj14, is an orange BBQ-sauce-style bottle with a white cap).
plan: Settled plan: top-down grasp of the bottle's cap/upper neck (the body at 6.1 cm is too close to the 7.7 cm opening, and the hand body would hit the cap if the grasp went lower), with fingers closing along world y (yaw -90, the home wrist orientation). Lift straight up to TCP z 0.32 so the hanging bottle's bottom (about 12.3 cm below the TCP) clears the basket rim by about 5 cm. Carry it over the liner's floor centre, lower until the bottle is inside the liner with its bottom a few cm above the floor, open, and retract straight up. Changes along the way: (1) I refined the grasp axis from wrist-camera depth of the cap top: (0.4018, -0.0797), cap top z 0.146. (2) I picked a grasp height of TCP z 0.125. The hand-body collision spheres start 1.8 cm above the TCP, so this put the pads on the cap without the palm touching it. (3) After the lift, held-object checks showed phantom collisions because the agent object stayed at its table position. I redefined the bottle as a synthetic full cylinder at its current hanging position, and did so again over the basket. (4) Perception re-detected the hanging bottle as a separate obstacle (obj21, later obj27), so I forgot it. (5) The basket model reported a 1.5-1.9 cm held-object overlap with a filled-in, camera-occluded liner wall. Point-based checks and the wrist and agentview images showed room, so I centred the bottle at (0.608, 0.266) between the measured liner walls. I lowered only to TCP z 0.19 (bottle bottom about 0.065) and checked the images before releasing.

steps.what: Read the embodiment, the instruction and the budget. Showed agentview and wrist images and annotated the object ids.
steps.why: Identify the robot, the salad dressing and the basket before moving.
steps.result: Panda with a 0.079 m gripper; 7990-step budget at control_dt 0.05. obj1 is the salad dressing bottle and obj7 the basket.

steps.what: Analysed obj1's points in height slices and the gripper's collision spheres (fk links, sphere_links).
steps.why: Choose the grasp height and width. Find how far the palm sits above the TCP, so the cap does not hit the hand.
steps.result: Body about 6.1 cm wide at z 0.02-0.07; upper part and cap about 3.5 cm at z 0.08-0.148. Finger spheres reach 2.2 cm below the TCP and the hand-body spheres start 1.8 cm above it. Chose a cap grasp with TCP z about 0.125.

steps.what: Mapped the basket with a heightmap of its points.
steps.why: Find the cavity centre, the rim height and the floor height for the release.
steps.result: Rim z 0.144, floor z about 0.01-0.02, cavity centre about (0.605, 0.26).

steps.what: Moved to a pre-grasp pose with the TCP at (0.402, -0.0795, 0.30), top-down, yaw -90, over 4.2 s (a 2.5 s preview was refused as too fast).
steps.why: Look down on the bottle with the wrist camera to refine the grasp axis.
steps.result: Done at step 90. The wrist depth gave the cap top at z 0.146, centred at (0.4018, -0.0797) and about 3.4 cm across; the TCP was within 1 mm of that axis.

steps.what: Merged perception's split bottle (body obj1 + cap obj13) into agent object obj17. Descended to TCP z 0.125 over 11.5 s (the preview min_duration was 8.6 s).
steps.why: Put the pads on the cap. Only finger spheres touched the bottle in check_batch, which the reference says overestimates the real fingers.
steps.result: Done at step 326. The agentview and wrist images showed the fingers straddling the neck/cap and the bottle still upright.
gripper_measured 0.536, gap 3.7 cm, below held_below 0.95, so the bottle was held. Step 356.

steps.what: Lifted straight up to TCP z 0.32 over 12.4 s, after a check_batch with the bottle as the held object.
steps.why: Raise the hanging bottle well above the basket rim.
steps.result: Done at step 610. The agentview showed the bottle hanging upright under the gripper with its old spot empty; the opening held at 0.540. Measured bottle bottom z 0.196, about 12.3 cm below the TCP.

steps.what: Fixed the held-object model. First transfer check_batch reported held-object collisions with the can and basket: obj17 was still at its table position. Defined obj23 as a synthetic full-bottle cylinder at the hanging position, replacing obj17 and the perceived hanging fragment obj21.
steps.result: The transfer check_batch was then contact-free. A warning said joint 2 passes near 0; the joint path was smooth and monotonic with no jumps, so I accepted it.

steps.what: Transferred at TCP z 0.32 to (0.605, 0.26) over 19 s.
steps.why: Carry the bottle over the basket's cavity centre.
steps.result: Done at step 999, with the opening still at 0.540. The agentview showed the bottle above the basket.

steps.what: Re-mapped the basket interior from both cameras. Re-anchored the held model over the basket (obj28) and forgot obj27, perception's copy of the hanging bottle. Scanned contacts by release height and x offset.
steps.why: Decide a safe release height and centring. check_batch reported a 1.5-1.9 cm held-object overlap with obj7 below TCP z 0.21.
steps.result: The real basket points showed no intrusion into the bottle cylinder at any release height. The overlap came from the mesh's filled-in, camera-occluded -x liner wall (about x 0.578). Annotated footprint rings in the wrist image sat inside the liner floor. Centred at (0.608, 0.266).

steps.what: Lowered to TCP z 0.19 over 5.65 s (bottle bottom about 0.065).
steps.why: Put the bottle inside the liner, below the rim, for a short drop.
steps.result: Done at step 1112. The agentview crop showed the bottle upright inside the liner, below the rim, still held (0.540).

steps.what: Opened the gripper (1 s) and held 0.5 s.
steps.why: Release the bottle into the basket.
steps.result: Opening read 0.023 (open). The bottle dropped about 4.5 cm and stood upright in the basket. Step 1142.

steps.what: Forgot the held model, re-perceived, checked the retract path, and retracted straight up to TCP z 0.30 over 4.3 s.
steps.why: Clear the gripper away without disturbing the bottle.
steps.result: Done at step 1228 with a contact-free path. The final agentview showed the bottle upright inside the basket and the other objects undisturbed. The wrist camera looked straight down on the cap at the basket centre.

steps.what: Final depth check with the wrist camera, then finish_episode.
steps.why: Verify the final state before ending, from two cameras plus depth.
steps.result: Cap top at z about 0.163, centred at (0.606, 0.266). The bottle bottom is about 0.02, on the liner floor, inside the basket footprint (x 0.55-0.67, y 0.19-0.335). Finished at step 1228 of 7990.

key_images.caption: Start: agentview with perception ids. obj1 = salad dressing (dark bottle, black cap) near the robot; obj7 = basket on the right.
Pre-grasp: wrist camera looking straight down on the bottle's cap, centred between the open fingers (TCP z 0.30).
Grasp height (TCP z 0.125): fingers straddle the bottle's neck/cap and the bottle is upright.
Fingers closed on the cap: measured opening 0.536 (gap 3.7 cm), so the bottle is held.
After the lift to TCP z 0.32: bottle hangs upright under the gripper and its original spot is empty.
Bottle carried at TCP z 0.32 to above the basket centre.
Bottle lowered into the liner (bottom about 0.065), upright and below the rim, just before release.
Final scene: salad dressing standing upright inside the basket; other objects undisturbed; gripper open and retracted.
Final close crop: the bottle's black cap and neck stand above the liner, with the body inside the basket.
Final top-down wrist view: bottle cap at the centre of the basket's liner (depth: cap top z about 0.163, bottom on the floor).

lessons: 1) This harness speed-limits motion near the objects heavily: a 17-20 cm vertical move needed a min_duration of 8.6-9.5 s. Preview first and rescale to about 1.3x min_duration. 2) Agent-defined objects do not move with the gripper. After lifting, redefine the held object at its current pose (a synthetic full cylinder works well) before calling check(held=...), or the stale geometry gives phantom collisions. 3) Perception splits a bottle into body and cap and re-detects a hanging held object as a new obstacle. Merge the parts with define_object and forget the duplicate. 4) Perception fills in camera-occluded walls (here the basket liner) and can report overlaps that are not there. Cross-check against the measured points and the wrist and agentview images before trusting or acting on them. 5) For a tall bottle on this Panda, a top-down grasp of the cap with the TCP about 2 cm below the cap top (the hand-body spheres start 1.8 cm above the TCP) held well, and lowering the bottle into the basket before a short drop left it upright. 6) Wrist-camera depth from directly above is good for refining a grasp axis to about 1 mm and for confirming the final height.
